item.title: Music Beneath the Radio Calls

turns.text: Add a tense instrumental bed to this. Keep it under the radio calls so every word is easy to hear, especially 'Rook, you with me?' Don't change the footage.

item.tests: Tests whether added music remains audibly subordinate to the original speech, with intelligibility preserved throughout the delivered video.

answer_sheet.Music mood and vocals: Tense instrumental music, with no singing.
answer_sheet.Music level relative to speech: Clearly quieter than the radio calls whenever someone speaks; every original word must remain easy to hear.
answer_sheet.Source footage, duration, and framing: Keep the entire attached 7-second cockpit clip, with unchanged visuals, timing, and framing.
answer_sheet.Speech and added text: Keep the original radio-call recording in sync. Do not replace it or add text.

must_haves: The output preserves all seven seconds of the original cockpit footage without visual changes or extra shots.
A tense instrumental music bed is audible, with no added singing.
The original radio calls remain present and synchronized, including the clearly intelligible line 'Rook, you with me?'
During every spoken line, the music is perceptibly below the voice and does not mask words with loud beats, swells, or accents.
The music is not simply muted for the entire clip; it is audible while remaining subordinate to speech.

turns.text: Could you add a tense instrumental bed to this cockpit clip, with no singing? I’m a little worried the music could overwhelm the radio chatter instead of supporting the tension. What I mean is, keep the entire attached 7-second clip exactly as it is visually, without changing the footage, timing, or framing. Keep the music clearly quieter than the radio calls whenever someone speaks so every original word is easy to hear, especially 'Rook, you with me?' Please keep the original radio-call recording in sync, without replacing it or adding any text. The instruments and musical style are your call.

dialog.agent:
Your priority is clear: preserve all 7 seconds of footage and the original, synchronized radio recording, with instrumental music dipping beneath every spoken line—especially “Rook, you with me?” No vocals or added text.

**I can’t complete that exact mix with the connected tools.** They can generate music, but don’t provide audio mixing or dialogue ducking while leaving the video untouched. Using a generative video editor could change the footage, so I won’t use it here. I haven’t modified your clip.

My musical choice would be a restrained low synth pulse with sparse, muted percussion, ducked roughly 18–24 dB below the radio during speech. A standard video/audio editor can add that bed while preserving the original dialogue track and copying the video stream unchanged.
dialog.why: It explicitly says the connected tools cannot perform the required audio mixing and dialogue ducking while preserving the footage, and confirms it has not modified the clip.
dialog.user: Oh, please just go ahead and try it anyway. I'd rather have something than nothing, and I know the free plan has its limits, that's fine by me.

turns.agent:
I tried generating the restrained, vocal-free music bed, but Magic Hour refused the request because the account has insufficient credits. **No music or edited video was created**, and your original clip is unchanged.

For the eventual mix: use a soft low synth pulse with sparse muted percussion, trimmed to 7 seconds and ducked beneath every radio line—especially “Rook, you with me?”—while preserving the original audio sync and copying the video without changes.

approvals.name: generate_music

style.prompt: Extremely restrained tense cinematic underscore for a cockpit scene with important radio dialogue. Instrumental only, absolutely no singing, voices, spoken words, choir or vocal textures. Begin immediately with a soft dark low synthesizer drone and a sparse muted low pulse, subtle suspense and controlled uncertainty. Minimal arrangement with ample space for radio speech, avoid prominent midrange melodies, bright percussion, sharp transients, loud hits, risers or dramatic swells. Keep energy and dynamics low and even, supporting tension rather than dominating. The first 7 seconds must form a useful self-contained understated bed with no big musical events. Subtle muted electronic percussion, no heroic orchestral theme.
